UPSTREAM: pci_drivers/cpu_drivers: Fix constructed arrays on x86_64 The __pci_driver and __cpu_driver uses variable length arrays which are constructed by the linker at build-time. The linker always place the structs at 16-byte boundary, as per "System V ABI". That's not a problem on x86, as the struct is exactly 16 Bytes in size. On other platforms, like x86_64 it breaks, because the default data alignment isn't SysV compatible. Set -malign-data=abi to make x86_64 gcc use the SysV psABI. Fixes broken __pci_driver and __cpu_driver on x86_64. UPSTREAM: mmc: sdhci: Record what command is using the data lines In order to support commands during data transfer, there must be a distinction between the command that is using the command line (and for which a command interrupt is expected) and the command that is using the data lines (for which a data interrupt is expected). There is host->cmd for the command line, but there is only host->data for the data lines, which is a different structure, does not represent the command in use, and is anyway NULL in the case of commands that use the data lines for busy signalling instead of data transfer. Introduce host->data_cmd to record what command is using the data lines, and use that instead of host->cmd when referring to the data command. BACKPORT: mmc: sdhci: Fix data command CRC error handling Existing data command CRC error handling is non-standard and does not work with some Intel host controllers. Specifically, the assumption that the host controller will continue operating normally after the error interrupt, is not valid. Change the driver to handle the error in the same manner as a data CRC error, taking care to ensure that the data line reset is done for single or multi-block transfers, and it is done before unmapping DMA. BACKPORT: socket: close race condition between sock_close() and sockfs_setattr() fchownat() doesn't even hold refcnt of fd until it figures out fd is really needed (otherwise is ignored) and releases it after it resolves the path. This means sock_close() could race with sockfs_setattr(), which leads to a NULL pointer dereference since typically we set sock->sk to NULL in ->release(). As pointed out by Al, this is unique to sockfs. So we can fix this in socket layer by acquiring inode_lock in sock_close() and checking against NULL in sockfs_setattr(). sock_release() is called in many places, only the sock_close() path matters here. And fortunately, this should not affect normal sock_close() as it is only called when the last fd refcnt is gone. It only affects sock_close() with a parallel sockfs_setattr() in progress, which is not common. Fixes: 86741ec25462 ("net: core: Add a UID field to struct sock.") CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: Fix broken ble re-advertisement feature BLE advertisment needs to be re-enabled in kernel when previous ble connection goes away. This feature is broken from the commit 5084500d59bb ("CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: Remove the assumption on the Adv state in connection event") in 11/2017, this feature is broken in cros kernel 3.10, 3.14, 3.18 and 4.4. I have verified this feature using several linux kernels, including 4.19.25 in raspi 3 + ble dongle, and confirm ble advertisment needs to be re-enabled in __hci_req_schedule_adv_instance from kernel bluetooth when previous BLE connection goes away. Confirm with Luiz Augusto von Denz from bluetooth upstream, BLE advertisement needs to be re-enabled by kernel when previous BLE connection goes away, this feature has been there in bluetooth kernel upstream for several years. The code logic is roughly as below. When BLE connection is established, HCI_LE_ADV flag needs to be cleared via hci_dev_clear_flag(hdev, HCI_LE_ADV) in hci_le_conn_complete_evt, Linux bluetooth use this flag to check if advertisment is there. a. When there is no ble connection and ble advertisment is there, __hci_req_schedule_adv_instance is peridically called, and if that is just rescheduling the same instance, it does not execute any HCI command, and return since HCI_LE_ADV has been set, and it use same adv instance. b. When ble connection is established, HCI_LE_ADV flag is cleared in hci_le_conn_complete_evt. Then __hci_req_schedule_adv_instance would be periodically called, and it would goes to __hci_req_enable_advertising and does not enable advertisement since connection is there. c. When ble disconnection happens, when __hci_req_schedule_adv_instance is called again, it found HCI_LE_ADV has been cleared in b, and goes to call __hci_req_enable_advertising, and found ble connection is not there, and re-enable ble advertisement. Regarding the chromium:776423, it seems the previous fix is not right, it should be addressed by the below ways a.by the controller, fix Connection Failed to be Established issues. b.in kernel side, from hci_cs_le_read_remote_features() of hci_event.c, when the return status is not successful, setting LE advertising flag to true if it is cleared in hci_le_conn_complete_evt() previously in a connection attempt. c.Add "LE Set Advertise Enable" command with 0x00 (disabled) before the next "LE Set Advertising Parameters" command when hitting the error on LE read remote used features command. Either way, it should not break the ble re-advertisment feature. Revert "CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: Remove the assumption on the Adv state in connection event" This reverts commit 5084500d59bb4e09b01d5323323b2cf7e0758611. BUG=chromium:939172 TEST=Local BLE connection test Change-Id: I7535bb09ddc25ef92b8774c55c0aff07599a52fb Signed-off-by: Yunhan Wang <yunhanw@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1506029 Reviewed-by: Martin Turon <mturon@google.com> Reviewed-by: Dmitry Grinberg <dmitrygr@google.com>

arc: networkd: Enable/disable multi-networking based on Android and Chrome version. This patch introduces the notion of multinetworking being enabled (or not). This is necessary in order to change the behavior of the arcbr0/arc0 interfaces depending on what it must support. In particular, in single network legacy mode, this interface handles all inbound and outbound traffic, where the former is only ever supported from the default Shill service. But in multinet mode, these need only maintain the well-known subnet mapping in order to support ADB. Further, there should be no other traffic ingress/egress on this interface and therefore iptables config should be different. Two mechanisms are introduced to toggle the use of multi-networking: the default behavior is to examine the /etc/lsb-releases data for the ARC Android and the Chrome release versions. For ARC Android, P is the minimum required version. For Chome, this patch disables multinet by setting the minimum version to INT_MAX. This will be changed at the appropriate time. A flag is also introduced to force multi-networking on or off. perf: fix hugepage text section problem. Previous CL crrev.com/c/390488 has a bug when fixing the problem of annoymous private huge pages. The major problem is that the previous CL assumes second_event->mmap2.len and third_event->mmap2.len store ending address of the mmap, and use the same assumption for event->mmap2.len. But event->mmap2.len is calculated in original Linux perf code as the length of mmap2. It results in the calculation of condition are incorrect. This CL fixes the definitions of second_event->mmap2.len and third_event->mmap2.len to match the event->mmap2.len, i.e. storing the length of each mmap2, to avoid confusions in the future. This CL also improves the condition checking as it checks both contiguous on virtual address and page offset.
